title: The Ridge's Shadow
story:
James walked deeper into the Lower Foothills as the morning mist began to part, revealing the steep, pine-studded shoulders of Cloudveil Ridge rising sharply against the sky. The dirt path narrowed beneath a dense canopy of dripping oak branches, and the familiar damp scent of the jungle floor gave way to the sharp, clean fragrance of mountain pine and wet stone. Every step took him further from the bustling streets of Oakhaven, replacing the distant echoes of cart wheels and church bells with the steady rush of a hidden mountain stream.

Stopping near an ancient, moss-covered stone marker by the side of the trail, James pulled the brass pocket compass from his cord and set it carefully upon his palm. He watched the needle spin and settle, pointing steadily toward the steep switchbacks that vanished into the upper tree line. He took a slow breath of the thin, cool mountain air, letting the quiet solitude of the ascent wash over him as he prepared for the climb ahead.

As the afternoon clouds gathered to cast long shadows across the valley, James found a sheltered rocky ledge beneath an overhanging boulder that offered a dry nook for the coming evening. He brushed away a light scattering of fallen pine needles, pulled his brass map canister and indigo wool close, and looked out over the vast green expanse of the foothills he had traversed all day. The world below felt impossibly distant, a quiet quilt of roofs and winding rivers fading into the blue twilight.
location: A sheltered rocky ledge in the Lower Foothills, ascending Cloudveil Ridge
